To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the gain and the lasing cross sections in GSGG: Cr:Nd crystals decrease with temperature, which makes it possible to achieve the required energy parameters in laser sources with GSGG crystals at a permissible temperature rise in the active medium.
the temperature dependence of the gain, lasing cross section, and losses in a ~1.064μ transition in GSGG: Cr:Nd crystals was studied in the temperature range of 80–300 K.
the temperature dependence of the gain in the 1.06μ laser transition in the gadolinium scandia gallium garnet: chromium, neodymium (Cr,Nd:GSGG) crystal was investigated in the 80–300K range.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the temperature dependence of gain and lasing cross section in a GSGG: Cr:Nd crystal at 1060 nm.
the study of the temperature dependence of the gain, lasing cross section, and other laser characteristics of the ~1.06-μ line of the GSGG: Cr:Nd crystal.

the development and application of a novel technique for the fabrication of a high-quality optical thin film with a thickness of several micrometers by means of the laser ablation of a solid material.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the temperature dependence of the lasing transition cross section in GSGG: Cr:Nd crystals is described by an expression that is similar to the expression used for the cross sections of lasing transitions in Nd-doped yttrium aluminum garnet crystals.

GSGG: Cr:Nd is the best material for the 1064 nm laser source.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the gain and lasing cross sections of a ~1μ transition in GSGG: Cr:Nd crystals are determined by the concentration of chromium and the temperature of the active medium.
the temperature dependence of the gain of GSGG: Cr:Nd is determined by the temperature dependence of its absorption and fluorescence cross section.
the GSGG:Nd:Cr laser is a very attractive candidate for the generation of tunable radiation in the 1.06μ range.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, at temperatures below ~200 K, the lasing cross sections are much larger than the gain cross sections, which makes it possible to achieve a high laser threshold.
the temperature dependence of the gain is determined by the gain cross section, which depends on temperature, and the resonance losses, which are proportional to the square of the gain cross section.
a GSGG: Cr:Nd laser with a 2.3% Nd concentration is a promising laser source in the near IR region.
